note: Analyst Shark · security angle. Findings only where the draft’s security posture fails a North Star criterion; out-of-scope hygiene is demoted or omitted.

findings.section: Wave 10 — Commission proposal; Wave 8 batch-confirm; Wave 9 envelope-confirm; Wave 17 confirm surfaces
findings.criterion: 3 — commission shows skill + seat + depth before spend; nothing runs until John confirms; confirmation records who · Statement — nothing is spent, written or started without a human confirmation
findings.message: The plan proves double-submit idempotence via `client_event_id` and records `who`, but never binds the confirmation to a **content-addressed snapshot of what was shown**. Confirm verbs mint `job_id` / commit scaffolding / open envelope against “the current proposal,” not against a hash (or immutable proposal version) of the skill + seat + depth + estimated spend John actually reviewed. Between render and confirm, any mutation of the proposal record (race, buggy rewrite, compromised caller of the single-writer spine) yields a launch or commit John never authorized. That is not “confirmed spend”; it is TOCTOU. Idempotence without integrity binding only stops *double* spend of whatever is live — it does not stop *wrong* spend. Every confirm path (commission, batch scaffolding, envelope) must refuse unless the confirm payload includes the proposal’s content hash / version and it still matches the ledger proposal; tests must prove a post-render mutation makes confirm refuse and launches zero.

findings.section: Wave 5 — G6 identity resolution; Waves 8/9/10 confirmation events
findings.criterion: 3 — confirmation records who · 9 — all of it passes with AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing
findings.message: G6 explicitly allows FAIL → `who = unattributed(shared_secret)` with only credential CLASS recorded, and “no IdP built.” Under that path, AUTH ON is a shared secret any holder can present: every spend/confirm is the same unattributable principal. Criterion 3’s `who` is then a decorative field, not an accountability control; criterion 9’s “auth ON outcomes” can green while any process with the token confirms commissions, envelopes, and scaffolding. The risk taxonomy already names auth-off green and unconfirmed spend — this is the sibling hole: **auth-on, zero attribution**. Either (a) FAIL is a hard HALT on any spend-confirm path until a recoverable subject exists, or (b) shared-secret mode is DEGRADED by name with a machine gate that still proves token presence/expiry/revocation *and* refuses to claim multi-principal `who`, and Wave 18 cannot stamp criterion 3 fully met under unattributed. As written, the plan normalizes a security non-answer as a recorded identity.

findings.section: Wave 1 auth-ON suite; Waves 8–10 confirm/spend; Wave 4 executor; Wave 18 kill gate
findings.criterion: 9 — AUTH ON, asserted on outcomes rather than plumbing · Statement — nothing is spent, written or started without a human confirmation
findings.message: Wave 1 adds negative auth cases (absent / expired / wrong-principal / revoked) and “one suite, no auth-off variant,” but later waves never require **auth revalidation at each authorization boundary**. Envelope debit (compiles/reflections), commission confirm, batch-confirm, and executor launch are the spend/write gates; if only the test harness starts under AUTH ON, a revoked or expired token mid-session can still deplete an envelope or launch a confirmed-shaped commission. That is plumbing-green auth, not outcome-asserted auth. Done-whens for Waves 4, 9, and 10 must include negative tests: revoked/expired/wrong-principal at the *confirm and launch* seams refuse with named states and zero pid / zero ledger append / zero envelope debit. Wave 18’s invariant sweep must assert those refusals on outcomes, not “suite ran with auth env set.”

findings.section: Wave 9 envelope bounds; Wave 10 estimated spend; Wave 4 executor
findings.criterion: 3 — skill + seat + depth shown before spend · Statement — nothing is spent … without a human confirmation · Risk taxonomy — unconfirmed spend
findings.message: Envelope hard-caps compiles (`$5` / 25 / 240m) with named exhaustion. Commissions are correctly excluded from the envelope and only *show* estimated spend — but nothing bounds or re-checks **actual** post-confirm spend against that estimate (or any commission ceiling). John can confirm a proposal stamped “~$2” and the executor can run a multi-hour trio burn with no second gate, no soft/hard refuse, and no named `spend-exceeded-estimate` state. Confirmation of an unbounded job is not confirmation of a known spend. The plan needs either a hard commission spend/time bound shown at confirm and enforced by the executor, or an explicit DEGRADED “estimate is advisory only” with a Wave-18 gate report name — not silent unbounded spend after a single confirm of a display-only number.

findings.section: Wave 6 single-writer spine; Wave 15 publishAttention / index delivery; Wave 16 High Seat
findings.criterion: 10 — roadmap_events has exactly ONE writer · 12–13 — projections / portfolio from correct project cells; campaign ledger is single source of truth
findings.message: “One writer” is a **module** invariant (no second append path). It is not a **tenant** invariant. The spine does not state that every append is authorized only for the resolved project root / project id of the authenticated session, or that `publishAttention` cannot target another project’s `attention` cell or event stream. Path escape tests (Wave 7/17) cover filesystem `..`/symlink for dossier artifacts; they do not cover forging a project key into the single writer so project A poisons project B’s roadmap or attention, which the High Seat then raises as `needs_you` / `deliverable_ready`. One writer with no project-binding check is a privilege-escalation seam across the portfolio surface criterion 13 trusts. Require project-scoped authz on every spine append + a negative cross-project write test (and a High Seat test that poisoned foreign writes never appear under the victim row).

findings.section: Wave 7 containment; Wave 13 handback → reflection / next-stage proposal; Wave 15 deliverable_ready
findings.criterion: 3 — commission proposed with skill + seat + depth before spend · 4 — reflection + next-stage propose→confirm · Risk taxonomy — scaffolding mistaken for commissioned plan; unconfirmed spend
findings.message: Wave 7 correctly treats handback **paths** as untrusted (escape-attempt → `path-escape-refused`). Wave 13 then feeds validated handback **content** into reflection receipts and model-funded next-stage PROPOSAL / compile. Validation is “6 campaign-memory fields” + corruption refuse — not integrity of semantics (skill steering, step ULID spoofing, inflated artifact claims). Bundle-hash gates `deliverable_ready` (good for badge integrity) but does not stop a malicious or buggy skill handback from shaping the next proposal text toward a different stage or skill. Skill selection is later table-bound at confirm — but free-text proposal content and Oranges prompts still drive what John is nudged to confirm. Security need: treat handback body as untrusted input into any model prompt; bind next-stage proposals to ledger step ULIDs and commissionable-skill rows only; refuse handbacks that name out-of-root or out-of-campaign identifiers even when paths parse cleanly; test that a handback cannot cause a proposal for a non-commissionable skill or unbound step.

findings.criterion: 2 — one confirmed session envelope covers compiles and reflections · 9 — AUTH ON
findings.message: Envelope-confirm is idempotent and records `who` once, but the plan never states that **only that principal (or that session)** may debit the envelope. Any concurrent authenticated caller sharing the project store could drain `ENVELOPE_MAX_SPEND_USD` / compile count after John opened the session. That converts a lightweight authoring budget into a shared spend pool. Bind envelope id to session + subject; refuse debit with a named state when caller subject ≠ envelope `who` (or when session id mismatches); test cross-session debit fails with zero spend.

findings.section: Wave 6 append idempotence; Waves 8/9/10 double-submit tests
findings.criterion: 3 — nothing runs until John confirms (confirm must succeed when John acts) · 10 — one writer with concurrency / identity semantics
findings.message: Caller-supplied `client_event_id` with “re-append is no-op” is necessary for double-click safety but, without server-minted nonces or HMAC binding id → principal + proposal hash, a peer who can write through the spine can pre-register John’s predictable confirm id and force his real confirm into “already-confirmed” with **no** real commit — or claim a no-op as success while state is wrong. Pair idempotency keys with authenticated, proposal-bound tokens issued at proposal render time; reject unknown or foreign ids with a named state distinct from already-confirmed.

findings.section: Wave 10 commission proposal render; dossier store
findings.criterion: 3 — show skill + seat + depth (not secrets) · 9 — AUTH ON outcomes
findings.message: Proposals must show seat family/depth; the plan never forbids persisting raw API keys, tokens, or driver secrets into proposal events, dossier fields, or chamber-rendered cards. A reviewable stage artifact that echoes env credentials violates least privilege and turns the campaign ledger into a secret store. Explicit allow-list of seat *metadata* fields; redaction test that secret-shaped values never appear in spine events or UI renders.
